correctness.rationale: Reconstructing Algorithm 1 exactly gives m1=lambda x0, B1=0, D1=sigma, d1=lambda x0/sigma and x1=(1-q)x0. The source bias correction gives m2=lambda x0(1-q/(1+beta)); inserting d1 and m2-m1 into the scalar B update yields B2=(eta lambda/(1+beta))(u/(u+epsilon))^4. Since u/(u+epsilon)<1 at every finite nonzero u, q<=1+beta implies B2<sigma, while solving B2>sigma for u gives the stated sharp threshold for q>1+beta. On the floor branch, x2=[1-2q+q^2/(1+beta)]x0. The frozen verifier replays the same recurrence and randomized parameter checks; it corroborates rather than substitutes for the algebra.
residual_risks: The official current implementation rescales epsilon in its constant-rebound branch; the audited theorem is correctly scoped to the paper's displayed recurrence, not every later implementation detail.

It does not expose a nonstandard structural lemma, an infinite-time phase diagram, or a boundary requiring more than routine substitution. Under the stated bar rejecting mechanically implied and tiny routine deductions, it does not retain sufficient independent value.

final_claim: For the defining paper's zero-initialized scalar Apollo recurrence, B2=(eta lambda/(1+beta))(u/(u+epsilon))^4; hence no finite initialization clears the curvature floor at the second informative step when q=eta lambda/sigma<=1+beta, while for q>1+beta the submitted explicit initialization threshold is necessary and sufficient.
